purpose: Adapt Expo's deferrable background callback into the same durable synchronization interface used by foreground and manual triggers: keep one hourly background task registered, deliver each background callback to coordinate-sender-sync as a budgeted background trigger, and observe the Background Scheduling Status for each Polling Run, raising a persistent Operator-action-required condition and one local notification when scheduling is restricted or unexpectedly unregistered.

inputs.name: minimum_interval
inputs.description: The desired hourly minimum interval between background callbacks: 60 minutes.

inputs.name: expected_registration
inputs.description: Registration is expected whenever the Sender has an active installation; the shell constructs this module only then.

inputs.name: execution_budget
inputs.description: The eight-minute soft work deadline within WorkManager's ten-minute execution window, delivered with each background trigger.

inputs.name: scheduling_platform
inputs.description: A seam over Expo BackgroundTask and TaskManager registration state and registration, combined with the operating system's background restriction.

inputs.name: background_callback
inputs.description: Each invocation of the registered task's executor by the operating system.

inputs.name: local_notifier
inputs.description: A seam that raises one health-data-free local notification naming an action-required scheduling condition.

inputs.name: sender_sync
inputs.description: coordinate-sender-sync@1's trigger, which receives each background trigger.

inputs.name: sender_storage
inputs.description: The Sender's SQLite database: this unit's scheduling state, behind the 3ug seam.

inputs.name: clock
inputs.description: The Sender wall clock for observation times.

outputs.name: registered_task
outputs.description: One persistently registered background task with a 60-minute minimum interval, registered only when missing and never replaced or removed.

outputs.name: background_trigger
outputs.description: Each background callback delivered as one background trigger with an eight-minute budget, reporting success only when the run checkpointed.

outputs.name: scheduling_observation
outputs.description: The available, restricted, or unregistered Background Scheduling Status observed for a Polling Run, recorded with its time; an observation, not a guarantee.

outputs.name: action_required_condition
outputs.description: A persistent restricted or unregistered condition, with one local notification at its onset, cleared when scheduling is observed available again.

observable_effects.name: background-task-registration
observable_effects.description: Registers the background task through the scheduling platform when it is missing; never unregisters it, replaces it, or requests a battery-optimization exemption or foreground service.

observable_effects.name: local-notification
observable_effects.description: Raises one health-data-free local notification at the onset of each action-required condition.

observable_effects.name: sender-storage-write
observable_effects.description: Applies this unit's Sender schema migration and writes only its own scheduling state.

owns: the background task's name, minimum interval, and register-when-missing rule
the eight-minute background budget and the background task's success or failure result
deriving the Background Scheduling Status from registration state and platform restriction
the persistent action-required scheduling condition and its notification rule
does_not_own: Polling Runs, trigger coalescing, deadlines, and checkpoints, which belong to coordinate-sender-sync
reading Health Connect, cursors, the Outbox, and health state, which belong to the reader and staging units
the Expo, TaskManager, notification, and background-restriction adapters, their package pins, and Android permissions, which the Sender shell enabling task provides
foreground and manual trigger adapters and Sender screens
presenting Background Scheduling Status, Polling Freshness, and staleness, which belong to the Portal
